candidates.title: Compare supplier confirmations with purchase orders

demandEvidence.chore: Compare supplier confirmation line items with the original purchase order, including SKU, quantity, price and delivery date.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: When a supplier confirmation contains dozens of line items, manually comparing every SKU, quantity, price, and delivery date against the original Purchase Order becomes time-consuming.

ease.reason: A beginner could compare synthetic line items in a spreadsheet, but no supplied reference supports document extraction or matching.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small online retailers handling many supplier confirmations might pay for review preparation; the post establishes no buyers or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can compare operator-entered sample rows and flag differences; document intake and accuracy remain untested.

autonomy.reason: A prototype could repeat field comparisons, while a person must verify source data and approve any purchase-order change.

evidence.reason: The post states a specific manual comparison task and its fields, but gives no frequency, rules or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Concrete chore is scorable, but provisional mean 5.2 is below threshold; no implementation reference is supplied.

candidates.title: Send a triggered email through Make

demandEvidence.chore: Send an email through an SMTP service when a trigger occurs in another app.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want a Make scenario to send an email through DigitalAka when a trigger occurs in another app.

ease.reason: A beginner can mock a trigger and test message, but no supplied reference supports provider setup or delivery.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent automation consultants may pay for setup help; the request establishes no service buyers or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can use a sample trigger and test inbox; live SMTP configuration and delivery remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A configured trigger might repeat the send, but a person must authorize credentials, verify delivery and handle failures.

evidence.reason: The request names provider email after another app trigger, but gives no volume, constraints or implementation evidence.

candidates.reason: The narrow mock is assessable, but provisional mean 4.6 is below threshold and this exact task has recent below-threshold assessments with no new implementation evidence.

candidates.title: Review business directory lead fields

demandEvidence.chore: Extract business directory information into lead-enrichment fields; the source title specifically includes a manager name and email.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I built an end-to-end n8n pipeline for DACH/German B2B lead enrichment that chains German directory scraping with an automated § 5 DDG Impressum extractor .

ease.reason: A synthetic business-only sample could be categorized, but the described workflow includes personal contact details and no supplied reference supports safe collection.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: professional-service firms may pay for business research, but this post offers a free workflow and establishes no paying buyers.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic-data demonstration is possible, but replicating scraped personal contact extraction would need authorization and privacy review.

autonomy.reason: A prototype could structure approved sample fields, while a person must check source permission, data minimization and each result.

evidence.reason: The post describes a specific directory-to-lead-enrichment workflow, but not repeated buyer demand or authorized data use.

candidates.reason: The described contact-harvesting workflow cannot be proposed as a service without evidence of authorized collection and appropriate privacy controls; the privacy-limited synthetic version is below threshold (4.2).
